To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the land use predicted by our model is consistent with the observed land use in the invariant region and that the land use in the variant region is highly dependent on the initial conditions of the simulation.
the land use in the invariant region of a model is almost certain, whereas the land use in variant region is uncertain and depends on path‐dependent processes and stochastic events.

(1) we have developed a methodology that allows researchers to identify the areas of a land‐use model's spatial domain where land‐use is almost certain and where land‐use patterns depend on a particular path of events; and (2) we demonstrate the application of our methodology on a land‐use agent‐based model and a multi‐temporal data set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to validate land‐use models.
how well an agent‐based model of land use performs, how to evaluate it, and the conditions under which it does or does not perform well.
how to validate spatially explicit land‐use models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model is accurate in some situations, and less accurate in others, but that it is possible to identify the situations in which the model is accurate and the situations in which it is less accurate.

, in the Washtenaw case, the land‐use model has high predictive accuracy in most of the county, but low predictive accuracy in the areas that are path dependent, i.e., where the land‐use type depends on particular events.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to validate a land‐use simulation, it is necessary to consider the model's process accuracy and the model's predictive accuracy.
we have developed a framework for evaluating agent‐based land use models.
the methods we describe provide a means to identify and quantify the extent to which a model is path dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of agent‐based models, the notion of model accuracy is complex and requires a more nuanced approach to validation.
, when validating agent‐based land use models, researchers should be explicit about the accuracy of the model in the invariant region and the variant region.

researchers should not be satisfied with simply showing that their model predicts well; they should also be able to show that the model's predictions are consistent with actual processes and that they can be validated using a variety of data sources.
